messages:
Morgan: running canary on dedicated-pool-4, getting a consistent 8-12% tail latency regression vs baseline after the flashautotune roll. looks tied to requests with KV cache hit + seq_len ~64-96. :thinking:
Sam: can you paste the perf profile / kernel picks?
Morgan: yeah, profiler snapshot from canary worker:
```
# profile snippet
seq_len=80, batch_size=4, head_dim=22, heads=32
active_kv_cache=true, kv_prefetch=on
chosen_kernel=flashv3_causal_tile32
fallback_path=sdpa_generic
gpu=sm92
avg_p99_latency_ms=143 vs baseline 129
```
Morgan: interesting bit: autotuner picked flashv3_causal_tile32 even though ffprobe shows heavy kv loads. fallback path triggers occasionally and spikes latency.
Jin: head_dim=22 is not a common divisor for many tile sizes, might force unaligned GEMM slices. autotuner probably scores flashv3 higher on raw throughput but forgets KV overhead.
Luis: can repro locally with a microbench harness. small script (python):
```
# repro harness
for seq in (64,80,96):
  run_inference(model='redwood-2', batch=4, seq_len=seq, head_dim=22, kv_cache=True)
```
Alex: any logs from kernel picker? maybe the scoring function doesn't include `kv_cache_active` penalty.
Morgan: here are the kernel-picker debug lines from the canary logs (sanitized):
```
[autotuner] candidates: [flashv1_noncausal, flashv2_causal_tile16, flashv3_causal_tile32, sdpa_generic]
[score] flashv1_noncausal -> 0.81
[score] flashv2_causal_tile16 -> 0.88
[score] flashv3_causal_tile32 -> 0.92
[score_adjust] kv_cache_active -> -0.15
[pick] flashv3_causal_tile32 (final_score=0.77)
```
Alex: oh, note final_score 0.77 > flashv2's 0.88? looks like scoring normalization bug (we multiply then subtract incorrectly).
Sam: nice catch. that would leave flashv3 selected even after kv penalty.
Jin: two things to fix: 1) scoring normalization so penalties reduce relative ranking correctly; 2) add a warmup probe that measures KV-driven small-kernel latency and apply a higher penalty for head_dim % tile != 0 combos.
Luis: propose a conservative quick fix: if head_dim % 8 != 0 and kv_cache_active then ban flashv3_causal_tile32 for canary. revertable flag: `autotune.experimental.disable_flashv3_unaligned_kv`
Morgan: sounds good. also noticed many of these requests use seq_len distribution with mass at 64-96 due to chat chunking -> affects which kernel is better. need sequence-length-aware scoring.
Alex: I sketched a heuristic to add to autotuner scoring. pseudo: 
```
score = base_throughput_score
if kv_cache_active:
  score -= kv_penalty_factor * (1 + head_dim_misalignment_ratio)
score -= seq_len_variance_penalty(seq_len_histogram)
apply_normalization()
```
Sam: can we get a quick A/B: run the scoring normalization fix + kv penalty on canary and compare p95/p99? I can wire a small patch.
Morgan: patch ready in branch `autotune/kv-aware-penalty` (PR up). dev-bot ran unit checks: all green. :white_check_mark:
dev-bot: CI pipeline: unit tests passed (24), integration smoke: flaky (1/3), canary rollout queued.
Jin: integration flaky likely due to nondeterministic fallback. we should add deterministic kernel pin test in harness.
Luis: I'll run local microbench with pinned kernels to validate baseline vs new scoring. dropping results into thread in ~30m.
Morgan: thanks. if A/B shows improvement, we should also add a telemetry tag `kernel_pick_reason` so product can see how often flashv3 was chosen despite kv_active.
Alex: agreed. also log `head_dim` and `head_dim % tile` in picker trace for future triage.
Sam: quick note — flashv3 has known larger register pressure on sm92 for tile32; combined with KV hits it increases L2 thrash. that aligns with our observed p99 spikes.
Morgan: OK action items: 1) Sam to push normalization fix + kv penalty (PR), 2) Jin add deterministic kernel pin test, 3) Luis run microbench and upload numbers, 4) Alex add picker telemetry fields. we will gate canary rollback if p99 > baseline by >5%.
Luis: uploading microbench csv now: https://internal/redwood/bench/2103456789-kv-head22.csv :eyes:
Morgan: nice, initial numbers look like p99 down from +9% to +1.5% after patch. schedule full canary. :rocket:
Sam: will start canary rollout at 16:30 UTC. will monitor `kernel_pick_reason` and `kv_cache_active` events.
Alex: if canary passes, follow-up to add a small model-specific profile table for head_dim oddities so autotuner doesn't relearn same cases.
Jin: thanks all. longitudinal note: we should expand autotuner probes to include small-kernel/kv-warm paths by default, not optional.
Morgan: agreed. good cleanup ticket: AUTOTUNE-963.
Morgan: closing the loop once canary finishes. :+1:
